attribution.note: Marcus's own X post, which he quotes and endorses in his own Substack post. Musk's prediction is only the target of the bet.

semantics.note: Offering a $1M bet and calling the idea 'absolutely absurd' is a firm negative expectation, so it counts as a scored forecast. The Optimus target, the best-humans threshold and the end-of-decade horizon are all kept.

contract.note: Reading 'end of the decade' as 2029-12-31 matches the 2029 in the quoted tweet. Requiring autonomous clinical superiority is the ordinary reading. Leaving out the 'at scale' wording favours neither side unfairly.

evidence.note: July 2026 UCSD preclinical surgery with teleoperated humanoids, not Optimus. It is relevant background only and says nothing about Optimus superiority.

reviews.rationale: The deadline is 2029-12-31, after the evaluation date. No Optimus clinical result meeting the early-resolution rule is in the packet. Not having shown the capability yet cannot support the claim early, so the forecast is not yet scorable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post.

semantics.note: Calling the idea 'absurd' is a firm negative expectation about robots in general. 'Anytime soon' is kept as the vague horizon.

contract.note: The 2029-12-31 deadline is inferred from the bet in the next sentence, not stated by Marcus. That is a reasonable and fairly generous reading of 'anytime soon'. The superiority threshold is the ordinary reading.

evidence.note: 2025 ex vivo autonomous surgical steps on gallbladders. This is progress, but there is no clinical comparison with top surgeons, so it does not contradict the claim.
2026 teleoperated humanoid surgery on animals. Teleoperated and preclinical, so it does not show autonomous superiority.

reviews.rationale: The inferred deadline (end of 2029) has not passed. The packet's examples of progress fall well short of the contradiction condition, so there is no early resolution. Current limitations cannot support the claim early either.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post.

semantics.note: 'Will surely' is firm, so this is a scored forecast with no deadline. Reading 'new date' as a later date fits the surrounding backpedaling context.

contract.note: The contract requires a renewed statement of the same surgical milestone with a later date. Republished old clips are correctly excluded, and treating the forecast as open-ended is fair. The 'retrospective' label is an error but does not affect the result.

evidence.note: January 2026 report of Musk's original three-year forecast. It predates Marcus's post, so it cannot show a later revision.

reviews.rationale: No verified statement from Musk after August 5, 2026 restating the surgery prediction with a later date was found. Because Marcus set no deadline, the absence of a revision so far is not failure. The claim stays open.

attribution.note: Marcus himself asserts 'didn't come to pass'. He paraphrases Musk's prediction, but the scored claim is Marcus's own statement about what happened.

semantics.note: This is a historical claim that AI had not exceeded the intelligence of all people by the end of 2025. The threshold and the date are kept.

contract.note: Reading the threshold as general superiority to the strongest humans is fair. The 'all humans collectively' reading is stronger, so whatever fails the individual reading also fails the collective one. In practice the ambiguity does not change the result.

evidence.note: ARC Prize assessment of December 5, 2025: AGI 'not yet'. An AI still beaten on tasks easy for ordinary humans has not exceeded every person.
Same assessment. It notes big 2025 gains but calls them still narrow in the global sense. That shows progress, not superiority, so it does not contradict the claim.
April 2024 report: Musk expected AI 'smarter than any one human' by about end-2025. It confirms the prediction Marcus paraphrased, not the outcome.

reviews.rationale: In December 2025 the benchmark organizer judged that AGI had not been reached and that AI capability was still narrow overall. Nothing in the packet shows broad superiority to the strongest humans by the end of 2025. The claim holds on the ordinary reading, though the evidence comes from one source dated early December.
